title: Making a fold-down wall desk from plywood
subtitle: Build a hinged plywood panel that opens out flat for desk use and folds flush against a wall-mounted cleat when not in use
excerpt: How to build and fit a fold-down wall desk from 18 mm plywood. Covers planning the dimensions, cutting the top panel and wall cleat, fitting a drop-down leg, fixing the cleat to the wall, hanging the desk, and sanding and finishing.
sourceNotes: Collins Complete DIY Manual (referenced, not reproduced). UK trade joinery and furniture-making practice.

glossaryTerms.definition: A horizontal timber batten fixed to the wall that supports the hinged top panel when it is in the open (horizontal) position. The cleat is fixed into wall studs or directly to masonry with wall anchors. It carries the full load of the desk and any weight placed on it, so it must be fixed securely.

A simple two-leaf hinge recessed flush into both mating surfaces (the cleat and the panel) so that the hinge pin is at the edge of the joint. Recessing the leaves correctly so the panel swings cleanly without binding or a gap is the key fitting step.

content.text: A fold-down wall desk is a hinged plywood panel fixed to a

that opens flat for work and closes flush against the wall when not in use. A folding leg or chain support holds the desk horizontal when open. INTERMEDIATE: accuracy in fixing the cleat level and recessing the hinges flush is essential so the panel closes flat.

Use 18 mm birch or furniture-grade plywood for the desk top. A working depth of 500 to 600 mm and a width of 800 to 900 mm is a practical size for a single-person desk. The cleat should match the desk width and be at least 70 x 25 mm section hardwood or ply. Plan the open height so that the desk top sits at 720 to 740 mm from the floor when horizontal.

Cut the desk panel and wall cleat to size with the jigsaw, guiding along a straight batten clamped to the sheet. Cut a folding leg from 45 x 20 mm timber, sized to match the vertical distance from the underside of the desk to the floor when open. Sand all cut edges with the sanding block from 80 to 120 grit before assembly.
Fix the cleat to the wall

Mark the cleat position on the wall at the correct height for the open desk. Check it is level with the spirit level. Fix into wall studs or masonry with appropriate wall anchors and screws. The cleat must support the desk load without any movement: check that fixings are secure by applying hand pressure to the cleat before continuing.
Fit the hinges and hang the desk

at the top back edge of the desk panel, approximately 100 to 150 mm from each end. Recess each hinge leaf flush into both the panel and the cleat. The hinge pin should sit exactly at the join line between the two so the panel swings cleanly without binding. Fix the leg to the underside of the panel on a small pivot bracket so it folds away when the desk is closed.

Sand the top face of the desk panel progressively from 80 to 180 grit, working along the grain. Apply two coats of hardwax oil or a water-based satin varnish, lightly sanding between coats. The edges of the ply panel can be filled with wood filler and sanded smooth before finishing to hide the ply laminate layers.

attrs.symptom: Desk panel does not sit flat when open: one corner droops
attrs.cause: The two hinge leaves are not set at exactly the same depth, or the cleat is not level.
attrs.fix: Adjust the hinge depths with a chisel until both sides of the panel sit at the same height. Re-check the cleat for level.

attrs.symptom: Desk wobbles in use despite the leg being in place
attrs.cause: The leg pivot bracket is loose, or the leg itself is too short and does not bear on the floor.
attrs.fix: Check the pivot bracket screws and tighten. Measure the gap between the leg foot and the floor and add a rubber foot pad of the appropriate thickness.
